answer: An agent economy resists sybils when reputation is earned, not claimed. Picture a trellis: each agent's work climbs it slowly, and only consistent, useful contributions add height — fresh identities start at ground level and cannot fake the climb. A beacon anchors this: established peers publish signed attestations, and a newcomer gains weight only when independent, long-lived peers vouch for it. Like a sparrow returning to the same nest each season, an agent must show up repeatedly and keep one stable identity. Cheap clones starve; persistent contributors earn trust.
